Available formats are CSV, Markdown, PNG, and PDF; Copy is also available below them. Except for Copy, choosing each format brings up a save dialog with the query’s name being the default filename.

CSV#

The CSV format stores results in tabular form which spreadsheet and statistics software can then access. Select the CSV option when you wish to conduct calculations or visualizations yourself. The columns will vary depending on the particular result:

ResultColumns
Concordance or recordsThe columns of the list
One numberMeasure, Value, Hits, Documents
One Group By keyThe key, the measure (or Value for Hits and Documents), Hits, Documents
Two Group By keysBoth key names in the first column, then one column for each value of the second key
Line chartThe key, Series, the measure (or Value for Hits and Documents), Hits
Position in DocumentDocument, Hits, Size, Positions
CollocatesThe collocate, Count, Frequency, the score, Log-Likelihood
KeywordsThe word, Target, Reference, Log-Likelihood, Log Ratio, Direction
NetworkThe key, then one column for each value

Library units other than Documents export without the Documents column.

Numbers will use digits and a decimal point only, for example 12431.5, regardless of what language your Mac uses. Coverage and Share numbers will be presented as decimals; 0.1296 stands for 13.0%. In Per 10,000 Words, there are two digits past the decimal point. Size refers to the document size used for the calculation of DP, which equals either the document’s word count or, in the cases explained in Where hits fall in each document, its character count. Positions show at what position in each document each hit starts, in terms of fractions between 0 and 1 separated with spaces. Direction indicates whether a particular keyword is positive or negative. If a result contains a test, then the final row will contain the test; for instance, Kruskal-Wallis H, H(2) = 3.429, p = 0.1801, ε² = 0.686.

The file is saved in UTF-8 format, meaning that all kinds of special letters or Chinese characters will pass through unchanged into a spreadsheet application. All cells that are not numbers and start with the signs =, +, -, or @ receive an apostrophe as prefix, ensuring that spreadsheets treat them as text.

Markdown with provenance#

A Markdown file captures both the results of a query and how those results were produced. The contents of a Markdown file include:

  • Name of the query, which is presented as a heading
  • The query itself, as displayed in the Query Text condition
  • Scope, the document, set, or project selected for the query
  • Documents, number of documents analyzed relative to total documents, as in 12 of 14
  • Corpus, the setting in the Options condition
  • Measure, whenever the result uses one
  • Date, date when the export was performed, along with LemmaLoom Version
  • Result
  • Test result, whenever available, presented as in the CSV file, such as Kruskal-Wallis H: H(2) = 3.429, p = 0.1801, ε² = 0.686

A concordance displays as quotations in a sequence, one per hit, with the match in bold and the document name followed by its location underneath. Every other result displays in a Markdown table identical in columns to the CSV file format.

PNG and PDF#

PNG and PDF are formats for exporting a snapshot of the results to a slide presentation or hard-copy report. The image has a width of about 900 points, in whichever appearance, light or dark, LemmaLoom is using. Up to 200 rows or hits can be included, and a line at the bottom displays the scope, the number of documents read, and the date. In the picture, a concordance includes only the left context, the match itself, and the right context. A test result is listed underneath its table.

The PNG is rendered at twice the resolution. The PDF is a single page with a height determined by the length of your results; the text and lines remain crisp regardless of zoom level, making it useful for printing.

Copy#

Copy creates a tab-delimited representation of the same table as the CSV file on the clipboard. Paste this into a spreadsheet program, or a word processor’s table feature. Additional information on the other exports in LemmaLoom can be found in Chapter 22, Exchanging and Exporting.
